St. Linus of Rome

St. Apostle Linus · Linus

Period
First century; exact episcopal dates and death circumstances not established here
Region
Rome
Titles / vocation
Apostle of the Seventy · Bishop

Introduction

St. Linus is named in the New Testament and remembered in Orthodox tradition as an early bishop of Rome after the Apostles.

Read the published life [1]

Biblical mentionEarly witness to episcopal successionLimits of the evidenceOrthodox commemorationChronology
Death / martyrdom

The cited primary and ecclesiastical notices do not establish his death

Read circumstances and sources

Biblical mention

The final greeting of Second Timothy includes Linus among Christians sending greetings. The verse supplies his name but does not provide a childhood, conversion story or detailed account of his ministry. Later identification with the bishop of Rome comes from the Church’s historical tradition.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · 2 Timothy 4:21

Early witness to episcopal succession

St. Irenaeus, writing in the second century, says that the Apostles entrusted the episcopal office of the Church at Rome to St. Linus. He explicitly identifies him with the Linus mentioned in the letters to Timothy. This is the source used when the lesson discusses the public succession of teachers and bishops.

[undefined] Source reading · Against Heresies III.3.3

Limits of the evidence

The cited OCA entry identifies his episcopal succession but does not describe his death. The account of martyrdom in the same group entry belongs to a different member of that group and must not be transferred to St. Linus. No execution method or exact death year is asserted here.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Individual notices; the St. Linus sentence is distinct from the martyrdom notice for Hermes

Orthodox commemoration

The OCA commemorates St. Linus on November 5 with other Apostles of the Seventy and names him a successor of St. Peter at Rome. The early witness concerns continuity of apostolic teaching and ministry; a one-sentence notice should not be expanded into an invented biography.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Title, commemoration heading and St. Linus notice
